title: Verify the chemical mechanism behind the red-wine-stain learning path (protein denaturation vs tannin/polyphenol chemistry)
question: What is the scientifically supported mechanism by which red wine stains set on and are removed from fabrics — is it protein denaturation and thermal cross-linking binding to the textile fiber as the ROTWEIN path claims ('ab 40°C beginnt Vernetzung, ab 80°C permanent fixiert', 'Heisses Wasser denaturiert Proteine'), or is it dominated by tannin/anthocyanin (polyphenol) interactions, and does hot water reliably worsen the stain or can it help?
why_now: PATH:SSF:CHE-REINIGUNG-ROTWEIN-0001 attributes red-wine stain setting to protein denaturation cross-linking with textile fibers and states sharp thermal thresholds (40°C onset, 80°C permanent fixation). Red wine's chromophores are polyphenols (anthocyanins, tannins), not proteins, and cotton is cellulose rather than protein, so the stated mechanism is likely a simplification with real teaching consequences. The module is prototype status; evidence-based correction would improve its chemistry claims before promotion.
real_world_anchor: Chemical mechanism of red-wine stain setting/removal on fabrics (tannin/polyphenol interactions vs protein denaturation) and the claimed 40°C/80°C thermal-fixation thresholds
